summary: Escalation: streaming responses disconnect (EOF/connection reset) during traffic spikes; correlates with overload in us-east
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports intermittent streaming disconnects during predictable traffic spikes. Symptoms are more frequent when using SSE streaming (chat/completions) vs non-streaming.
- Observed by customer as: abrupt end of stream (EOF), "connection reset by peer", or occasional 502 from their edge when our upstream closes.

Impact
- Customer experiences partial responses and has to re-issue requests, increasing cost and user-facing errors.
- Customer escalation: executive visibility due to reliability expectations for a launch.

Customer details
- Company: PulseStack
- Use case: customer-facing chat with streaming UI; bursts at the top of the hour (job triggers + user traffic).
- Request shape: long prompts (8k–20k tokens input), streaming enabled, max_tokens typically 1k–2k.

Environment
- Hosted API production
- Regions: us-east primarily; intermittent similar behavior in eu-west during global spike windows.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided)
1) Run 200–400 concurrent streaming chat requests with long prompts.
2) Observe disconnects clustered during 2–5 minute spike windows.
3) Non-streaming requests in same window tend to return 503/timeout; streaming more often disconnects mid-response.

What we saw (initial triage)
- Internal dashboards showed elevated queue depth + GPU pool saturation around the same timestamps.
- Increased upstream cancellations/aborts in the runtime during decode scheduling, consistent with overload protection gaps (pre-flag).
- Customer reported no consistent Retry-After semantics (disconnects do not include HTTP status).

Customer log excerpts (sanitized)
- 2025-11-22T18:03:41Z: "httpx.RemoteProtocolError: Server disconnected without sending a response" (Python)
- 2025-11-22T18:03:44Z: "EOF while reading event stream" (Node fetch/SSE)
- 2025-11-22T18:04:02Z: 502 from customer edge: "upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header"

Ask from customer
- Clarify whether these are overload-related, provide actionable retry guidance, and confirm roadmap for deterministic overload behavior (429/503 + Retry-After) rather than ambiguous disconnects/timeouts.
comments: 2025-11-22 18:27 UTC (Dev Patel - Support): Acknowledged escalation. Requested request IDs + timestamps + region + model + whether they retry/reconnect automatically. Shared temporary guidance: treat disconnects as retryable with exponential backoff + jitter; cap concurrent streams; consider non-streaming for critical flows until stabilized.

2025-11-22 19:10 UTC (Customer - PulseStack): Provided 35 request IDs and a graph of disconnect rate peaking at ~6% during 18:00–18:07 UTC. Confirmed they currently retry immediately (no jitter) and may open >1 retry in parallel per failed stream.

2025-11-22 19:34 UTC (Owen Phillips - Support): Pulled traces for sample request IDs. Pattern: elevated time-in-queue, then stream abort mid-decode. Noted many client reconnects within <200ms (retry storm risk). Looping in SRE for overload correlation and guidance on safe Retry-After values / recommended client behavior.

2025-11-22 20:05 UTC (Rafael Mendes - SRE): Correlated to us-east GPU pool saturation + scheduler queue blowup. During overload, runtime can abort existing streams (not just reject new work), leading to disconnects that do not map cleanly to HTTP errors today. This is exactly what the Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding work is intended to fix (early shed at gateway + bounded queues). Proposed immediate mitigation: shift a portion of traffic to eu-west, and limit concurrency per API key for streaming routes temporarily.

2025-11-22 20:22 UTC (Christine Wong - SRE): Confirmed we can enable overload protection feature flag for the customer’s route in us-east canary (edge admission + standardized error response where possible). For mid-stream aborts, we still may see disconnects until runtime bounded-queue changes are fully rolled out. ETA for runtime queue bounding in us-east canary: early next week.

2025-11-22 21:03 UTC (Dev Patel - Support): Sent customer interim guidance (below) and asked them to confirm they can implement jitter and cap retries. Also asked them to add a unique request header for correlation on retries (e.g., X-Client-Request-Id).

2025-11-25 17:40 UTC (Rafael Mendes - SRE): Runtime bounded queue + early shed deployed behind flag in us-east canary. Expected change: fewer mid-stream disconnects; more deterministic upfront 429/503 with explicit overload codes + Retry-After on new requests when breaker opens. Monitoring for flapping / regressions.

2025-11-27 16:12 UTC (Owen Phillips - Support): Post-change check for customer’s org: disconnect rate down from ~6% peak to <0.8% peak during comparable spike window; overall error rate mostly shifts to 429 with Retry-After: 2–5s. Noted one customer-side issue: immediate retry loop without jitter still causes bursts; recommended backoff policy reiterated.

2025-12-03 19:18 UTC (Customer - PulseStack): Confirmed they added exponential backoff with jitter and reduced max concurrent streams per worker. Reported "significant improvement"; still sees occasional 503 with Retry-After, but can handle gracefully. Asked whether shed errors are billed.

2025-12-04 00:06 UTC (Owen Phillips - Support): Confirmed overload-shed responses are not billed for tokens (no generation performed). For partial streams that disconnect after some tokens, usage may reflect generated tokens up to disconnect; advised logging usage where available and opening a billing inquiry if anomalies are observed. Linked them to support FAQ draft guidance and reiterated best-practice retries.

2025-12-05 18:30 UTC (Dev Patel - Support): Marking resolved. Customer stable with retry/jitter + reduced concurrency. SRE monitoring continues as overload protection expands; will proactively notify if behavior changes during global rollout.
resolution:
Root cause
- Overload conditions (GPU pool saturation + queue blowups) caused mid-stream aborts in the runtime during decode scheduling. Because the connection is already established for streaming, the failure often surfaced as an abrupt disconnect (EOF/reset) rather than a clean HTTP error.

Mitigation / Fix
- Enabled staged overload protection controls in us-east (canary): edge admission + routing/capacity-aware breaker behavior where applicable.
- Deployed runtime bounded queue + deterministic shed at scheduler boundary behind feature flag, reducing mid-stream disconnects and shifting failures to deterministic 429/503 on new admissions.
- Provided customer retry/backoff guidance to prevent retry storms.

Customer-facing workaround guidance (shared)
- Treat disconnects/EOF as retryable; do not retry immediately.
- Use exponential backoff with jitter; start at 250–500ms, cap at ~10–20s; max 3–5 retries depending on UX.
- Respect Retry-After header when present (do not override).
- Avoid parallel retries for the same user request; ensure a single in-flight retry chain.
- Reduce max_tokens during peak windows and cap concurrent streaming requests per worker.
- Consider failover to non-streaming mode for critical flows when high reliability is required.

Follow-ups
- Track ongoing rollout of standardized overload error semantics and SDK surfacing of Retry-After / Redwood overload codes (see linked PRs).
internal_notes: Support should watch for similar reports after rollout: customers interpreting new 429s as "rate limiting" rather than overload shedding. Point them to Retry-After semantics and recommend jitter. If customer is seeing 429 spikes but also has aggressive retries, request client retry policy and confirm no infinite retry loops. Reference: #support and #incidents threads for INC-2025-11-22-USE1-STREAM-OVERLOAD.
